findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top convergence gene, but in Gubatan 2026 neutrophils make nearly all of its inflamed-mucosa transcripts [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]. Smillie (no neutrophils) assigns it to T/NK cells and the second dataset to myeloid, so the attribution does not replicate and the Smillie call is an artefact of missing neutrophils. After composition adjustment the change falls from [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; unadjusted_log2fc=2.5984] to [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409] (partly_composition, still significant): mainly a marker of neutrophil influx; drug action would be on neutrophil recruitment, not a tissue-intrinsic change.

CXCR1 is also almost entirely neutrophil-derived in inflamed UC mucosa [gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962]; its bulk rise should be read as neutrophil influx, like CXCR2.

CXCL8 is made mostly by myeloid cells in Smillie (replicated in the second dataset), and neutrophils carry a large share in Gubatan [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]. After composition adjustment the change is no longer significant (verdict composition) [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0523]: a marker of myeloid/neutrophil influx; the adjustment may over-correct if resident cells are activated, so this is not proof of pure influx.

MMP1 comes from stromal cells, mainly inflammatory fibroblasts [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.531], and the stromal attribution replicates in the second dataset. Little is neutrophil-derived and the change stays significant after adjustment [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636] (partly_composition): a tissue-intrinsic fibroblast programme.

DUOX2 is almost wholly epithelial (enterocytes) and replicated in the second dataset [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947]. It keeps a significant change after adjustment [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161] (partly_composition), supporting an intrinsic epithelial change.

CHI3L1 is attributed to inflammatory fibroblasts in Smillie [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.652], replicated as stromal in the second dataset, though neutrophils also carry a sizeable share in Gubatan (caveat). The change survives adjustment [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967] (partly_composition).

IDO1 is myeloid (macrophages, DC1; replicated) with epithelial contribution and almost no neutrophil origin [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.072]. The change stays significant after adjustment [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505] (partly_composition).

CD274 (PD-L1) is dispersed in Smillie (plasma, macrophages, enterocytes; myeloid replicated) but neutrophils make a large share in Gubatan [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]. A modest change remains after adjustment [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978] (partly_composition); cell-of-origin is ambiguous.

S100A8 is predominantly neutrophil-derived [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]; a reduced but significant change remains after adjustment [gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231] (partly_composition). It is a neutrophil-influx marker rather than a cell-type target.
AQP9 is overwhelmingly neutrophil-derived [gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92], so its high rank reflects neutrophil arrival.

In situ, CXCR2 agrees with the neutrophil attribution and contradicts the Smillie T/NK call: in Xenium inflamed sections neutrophils carry [gene=CXCR2; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:GSE312420; attribution_by_state.inflamed.neutrophil=0.365] of its transcripts, and in deconvolved Visium spots Neutrophil is the top expresser [gene=CXCR2; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.386]. High spots are significantly enriched for neutrophil neighbours and Xenium neighbours are neutrophil-enriched. Negatives: raw Visium spot correlation is weak and neutrophil is first in only one of two UC sections, and CosMx detects CXCR2 only at background (best lineage T_NK, not above background), so spatial support rests on Xenium and deconvolution.

In Visium, deconvolution assigns most CXCL8 signal to neutrophils [gene=CXCL8; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.609], while the composition-corrected source is Myeloid (consistent with Smillie macrophages); high spots are surrounded by neutrophils, inflammatory fibroblasts and myeloid cells. The raw spot-level lineage association (myeloid first, fibroblast second) is not consistent across sections [gene=CXCL8; type=spatial_visium; source=DATASET:GSE189184; p_sections=0.142], CosMx is at background and the gene is not on the Xenium panel: the in-situ source is neutrophil/myeloid but only weakly resolved.

MMP1 in situ agrees with the single-cell fibroblast attribution: the deconvolved Visium top expresser and composition-corrected source is Inflammatory_fibroblast [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.579]; its high spots are enriched for inflammatory fibroblasts and also neutrophils, consistent with a fibroblast-neutrophil niche. Not on the Xenium panel and CosMx is at background.

DUOX2 is the best-confirmed gene in situ: epithelial cells carry [gene=DUOX2; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:GSE312420; attribution_by_state.inflamed.epithelial=0.921] of its Xenium transcripts in inflamed sections, and Epithelial is the sole deconvolved Visium expresser [gene=DUOX2; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.812]; Visium lineage association is epithelial-first in all UC sections analysed. Xenium, Visium and single-cell all agree.

CHI3L1 in situ only partly agrees with the fibroblast attribution: the raw top deconvolved expresser is Plasma [gene=CHI3L1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.258], with Inflammatory_fibroblast a close second, but the composition-corrected source and the neighbours of high spots favour inflammatory fibroblasts, with endothelial, plasma and myeloid cells also enriched. CosMx shows fibroblast as best lineage but not above background; not on Xenium. Fibroblast origin is supported, not exclusive.

IDO1 in situ disagrees with the myeloid attribution from single-cell data: Xenium inflamed sections give epithelium the largest share [gene=IDO1; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:GSE312420; attribution_by_state.inflamed.epithelial=0.371], and the Visium top expresser is Epithelial [gene=IDO1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.349] with T_NK close behind, although the composition-corrected source is Myeloid. Xenium neighbours are lymphoid and neutrophil rich. Visium spot correlations are weak, so the producing cell (epithelial versus myeloid) is unresolved and an epithelial IDO1 programme is plausible.

S100A8 in situ agrees with the neutrophil origin: Neutrophil is the top deconvolved Visium expresser and composition-corrected source [gene=S100A8; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.632], and high spots are surrounded by neutrophils, inflammatory fibroblasts and myeloid cells. Not on Xenium; CosMx is at background.

CD274 has no resolved in-situ source: it is not analysed in Visium spot analysis (too few spots), not on Xenium, CosMx is at background, and deconvolution gives a weak epithelial top contribution [gene=CD274; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.234] against a composition-corrected source of Myeloid, with no cell group enriched around high spots. Negative result: the spatial data neither confirm nor refute the myeloid/neutrophil attribution.

caveats: Composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells become activated; loss of significance (CXCL8) is not proof of pure influx.
Shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance; Smillie lacks neutrophils so its lineage calls for neutrophil genes (CXCR2) are unreliable.
Composition was checked only for CXCR2, CXCL8, IDO1, MMP1, DUOX2, CHI3L1, CD274 and S100A8.

Spatial data are limited: Visium spots hold several cells and only a few UC sections support each gene; CosMx detects all eight queried genes only at background, so it was not used to attribute cells; Xenium covers only CXCR2, DUOX2 and IDO1 of the genes queried (two sections left out for low counts).
